v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1180→1260 monthly, E-07), driven primarily by the "billing import + validation" step of meter-to-cash issuing incorrect bills from accepted ACTUAL meter reads rather than by slow dispute handling (E-01, within SLA) or missing reads (majority of disputed bills, 1785/3025, are ACTUAL-type, not ESTIMATED, E-03). The best-supported mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is a change to billing import validation rules around August that misclassifies or mis-rates valid accepted reads into wrong bills, producing the dispute surge.
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07), coincident with validation rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13). BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw AMI register readings directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13); AMI firmware v4.2, rolled out 2026-06, reports register readings in 0.1 m3 units versus older firmware's whole m3 units (E-14), so BV-17 misreads normal v4.2 consumption as a ~10x spike. This causes billing import validation to reject valid, on-time AMI reads as "high consumption" and substitute an estimate instead: 1184 of the 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts show exactly this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern tagged firmware v4.2 (E-12). The resulting wrong estimated bills drive at least this AMI-metered portion of the surge; response-handling speed is within SLA (E-01) and no tariff change occurred (E-04), ruling out those alternatives. The mechanism behind the larger ACTUAL-read-type dispute share (1785/3025, E-03) is not yet confirmed and is flagged as an open unknown.
